newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian bourse slows, but interest lingers.
newsitem.headline: Estonian bourse slows, but interest lingers.

text.p: Estonian shares slowed down on Friday after a couple of days of relatively healthy activity but dealers said prices would hold around current levels with some pent-up demand among investors.
The Talse index rose 0.71 percent to 262.93 with 45.9 million kroons traded on the main list.
"Today's trade also released some of that pent-up demand of recent weeks and encouraged speculative interest," one dealer said, noting it was still a relatively quiet market.
Tallinna Pank was most active on 11.9 million kroons, gaining 1.15 kroons to close on 58.10 kroons.
"One big lot of 60,000 shares was moved in Tallinna Pank, but it looked like a dealer filling a client's order and may have been left over from Thursday," a dealer said.
Hansapank saw 11.8 million kroons change hands to move 1.35 kroons higher to close at 139.65 kroons.
Hoiupank saw 11.2 million kroons traded to slip to 136.06, 0.44 kroons lower compared to Thursday's close.
Both have been at the centre of merger speculation. Hansa said it was seeking a partner to help it expand into Lithuania while Hoiu said it would consider merging with any local bank.
"The talk of possible mergers is just an early start to the expected merger process in Estonia," one trader said.
"The recent activity on the bourse has more to do with having a market that suits speculators," another dealer said.
Trade on the free market was 5.9 million kroons on Friday with Norma the most active at 4.95 million kroons, adding 1.5 kroons to 71 kroons.
